purpose: Regorafenib is used to treat certain types of cancer, including colorectal cancer that has spread, gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST), and liver cancer (hepatocellular carcinoma). It is typically used when other treatments have not worked or are no longer working. Your doctor chose this medicine because it targets specific proteins that help cancer cells grow.
how_it_works: Regorafenib works by blocking special proteins called kinases that cancer cells need to grow and spread. Think of it like cutting off the cancer's fuel supply — it stops the signals that tell cancer cells to multiply and form new blood vessels that feed the tumor. By blocking these signals, the medicine helps slow down or stop the cancer from growing.
common_side_effects: Fatigue and weakness, hand-foot skin reaction (redness, pain, or blisters on palms and soles), diarrhea, decreased appetite, high blood pressure, mouth sores, weight loss, hoarse voice, infections, and stomach pain. Most patients experience some tiredness and skin changes on their hands and feet.
warnings: This medicine can cause serious liver problems — your doctor will check your liver with blood tests regularly. It can also cause severe bleeding, heart problems, or a rare but serious condition called RPLS that affects the brain. Do not take it if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, as it can harm the baby. Tell your doctor right away if you notice unusual bleeding, yellowing of your skin or eyes, chest pain, or severe headaches. Avoid grapefruit while taking this medicine.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 160 mg (four 40 mg tablets) taken by mouth once a day for the first 21 days of every 28-day cycle. Take it at the same time each day with a low-fat meal. Swallow the tablets whole — do not crush or break them. Your doctor may lower your dose if you have side effects.
